USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Localizing an aspirated object

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A child abruptly becomes hoarse and develops inspiratory stridor after placing a bead in her mouth. Breath sounds are not distinctly asymmetric. Which location is more consistent with these findings than with a focal expiratory wheeze?

  1. Larynx or upper trachea
  2. Right main bronchus
  3. Left main bronchus
  4. Right middle-lobe bronchus
  5. Left lower-lobe bronchus
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Larynx or upper trachea

Voice change and stridor favor a proximal airway obstruction.

Understanding the options

Larynx or upper trachea
Voice change and stridor favor a proximal airway obstruction.
Right main bronchus
Main-bronchial impaction more often produces asymmetric air entry or focal wheeze rather than voice change and stridor.
Left main bronchus
A bronchial object more often produces unilateral lower-airway findings.
Right middle-lobe bronchus
A lobar obstruction causes focal lung findings and does not readily explain acute hoarseness.
Left lower-lobe bronchus
A distal lobar location is less consistent with an inspiratory upper-airway sound and voice change.
